results.fixture: Native browser CORS PUT/GET/HEAD; byte equality; server verification; persisted passed result; missing CORS rejects; failed DELETE preserves exact cleanup responsibility; retry succeeds; leaving without completion followed by controlled persisted expiry invokes real server maintenance and ends with an empty object list.
results.realServices: R2 and SeaweedFS connection tests passed. Authenticated wrong-Origin HTTP requests were rejected before creating probes. Native browser PUT/GET/HEAD all returned readable cors responses. Server verification/delete, reload persistence, exact-key HEAD 404 and empty storage-prefix ListObjects all passed.
results.credentialScan: All 9 JSON/log evidence files across fixture and both real-service rounds contain no configured credential values or complete signed URLs.

limitations: API-driven browser probe proves protocol and application endpoints. It does not invoke the production React cors-transport via UI clicks and is not UI/design acceptance.
Failure and expiry injection was local HTTP fixture plus the disposable database; cloud Bucket policies were not changed.
The fixture does not validate AWS signatures. Only R2 and SeaweedFS runs prove the real-service signature/browser protocol.
Current task UI requires separate approved design integration, real page screenshots, independent design review and human acceptance.
Physical devices, alternative browser engines, release images and AMD64/ARM64 containers were not tested.
